credentials.name: MSSC CPT 4.0
credentials.signals: Foundational production competency across safety, quality practices, manufacturing processes, and maintenance awareness. A good baseline for entry-level roles; not a substitute for role-specific technical depth.
credentials.note: Source: MSSC Candidate & Certificant Handbook v18 (2024), 'Assessment Content Outline (Work Standards)' section. Weighting = exam content-area weighting (% of assessment questions), not a stated importance ranking. Green Production is an optional 5th module, not required for full CPT certification.

modules.name: Safety
activities: Work in a Safe and Productive Manufacturing Workplace
Monitor safe equipment and operator performance

modules.name: Quality Practices & Measurement
activities: Inspect materials and product/process at all stages to ensure they meet specifications
Use common measurement systems and precision measurement tools
Participate in periodic or statistically based internal quality audit activities

modules.name: Manufacturing Processes & Production
activities: Set up and verify equipment for the production process
Prepare final product for shipping or distribution
Determine resources available for the production process
Coordinate workflow with team members and other work groups

modules.name: Maintenance Awareness
activities: Recognize potential maintenance issues with basic production systems, including knowledge of when to inform maintenance personnel about problems
Perform preventive maintenance and routine repair
Monitor indicators to ensure correct operations
Perform all housekeeping to maintain production schedule

modules.name: Green Production (optional add-on)
activities: Use advanced materials in production to reduce weight and increase life
Monitor environmental aspects at each stage of production
Reprocess materials by recycling and reuse throughout product life cycle to optimize waste reduction
Implement and promote environmental programs, projects, policies or procedures
Conduct environmental incident and hazard investigations

credentials.name: Polymechanic / Advanced Manufacturing Technician
credentials.signals: Broad, multi-domain technician capability across mechanical, electrical, controls, quality, and digital systems, validated against employer-defined competencies rather than seat time. The strongest single signal for a modern multi-skilled technician role.
credentials.bestFor: A role that has converged several formerly separate jobs, or that spans mechanical, electrical, controls and quality work at once.
credentials.text: multi-skilled technician mechanical electrical controls automation robotics quality digital systems troubleshooting diagnostics preventive maintenance instrumentation sensors drives motors programmable logic controllers cross-training convergence employer-defined competencies polymechanic advanced manufacturing technician mechatronics

credentials.name: Registered Apprenticeship (INCAP or another sponsor)
credentials.signals: Structured on-the-job learning plus related technical instruction, ending in a nationally recognized credential. The right answer whenever a requirement is real but a candidate could reasonably earn it while employed.
credentials.bestFor: A requirement that is genuinely necessary but that a motivated hire could earn on the job rather than arrive with.
